Rugged tablet for Payaca

Payaca is job management, quoting and invoicing software built and sold from Bristol by Payaca Ltd. The UK site now describes it as a CRM, job management and field service system for clean tech installers, naming solar, heat pump, battery storage and EV charging, and lists proposals with online e-signatures and deposits, map-based scheduling, site surveys, MCS handover documents, DNO applications, job costs, stock, invoicing and Xero and QuickBooks sync. The office runs all of that in the web app; the engineer or installer on site uses the Field Service by Payaca app on a phone or tablet.

The Field Service app is where the site work happens. The vendor's Google Play listing describes a day's scheduled events, time tracking for travel, work and admin, a materials list for each job, directions and ETA messages to the customer, checklists and forms, photo and file uploads, and an offline mode that syncs when the connection returns. The vendor's own update notes add that documents can be generated and signed by the customer on site without a signal, that materials are stored on the device, and that photos, videos and documents can be attached to custom fields from the app. That is a device that goes on roofs, into plant rooms and lofts, and gets handed to a customer to sign, which is where an unsealed consumer tablet tends to fail early.

This page sets out what Payaca publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged devices meet those published requirements, where the Windows tablet fits and where it does not, and how a UK installer can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet. Where the vendor publishes nothing, we say so rather than guess.

Requirements

What Payaca needs from a device

Each item below comes from Payaca Ltd's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 7.0 or later from Google Play; no RAM or storage figure published

    Payaca publishes no system requirements page. The only Android figure is in the Google Play listing data for Field Service by Payaca, which gives a minimum API level of 24, which is Android 7.0. For context, the App Store listing says the app needs iOS 16.4 or later on iPhone and iPadOS 16.4 or later on iPad, and is 79.5MB. No RAM, storage or processor figure is published for phones or tablets, and no screen-size guidance. Help centre articles about the app that appear in search results (help.payaca.com) returned a page not found message when checked on 19 October 2026, and the help centre home address redirects to the web app login, so the figures here come from the store listings, the vendor's features page and its updates pages. Source: play.google.com

  • Android app from Google Play: Field Service by Payaca

    The current Android app is Field Service by Payaca (package com.payaca.fieldservice.mobile, developer shown as Payaca, with PAYACA LIMITED and a Bristol address in the developer details). When checked on 19 October 2026 the listing showed version 1.32.0, updated 15 July 2026, 100+ downloads, a PEGI 3 rating and the interactive elements Users interact, Shares location and In-app purchases. The listing as fetched did not show Phone or Tablet device chips, so we cannot say the vendor publishes a tablet layout; the App Store listing does name iPad. An older app, Payaca mobile app (package com.payaca.mobileapp), is the one the vendor's 2022 update notes link to; its 2025 and 2026 updates refer only to the Field Service app, so that is the one to install. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline working, with the day's events and materials stored on the device

    The vendor's mobile app page says the app is built offline-first, gives full functionality without internet, and syncs when back online. Its update notes are more specific: on first opening, the app saves that day's and the next day's events and some upcoming tasks to the device, with a refresh button (2 November 2022); the materials available to the user are stored on the device so a materials list can be built offline (1 November 2024); confirming you are on the way, starting work and completing an event now work more reliably without a stable connection and sync later (21 August 2025); work time logs can be started and ended repeatedly while offline (29 September 2025); and generating a document, filling it in and capturing a signature all work without a signal (12 June 2026). The vendor does not publish how much storage the cached data needs. Source: payaca.com

  • Photos, videos and files uploaded from the app, including large batches

    The Google Play description lists uploading photos and files for job documentation, and the mobile app page says engineers take photos within a job, annotate them with notes or markups, and that pre-installation, progress and completion photos attach to the project record. The vendor's update notes say uploads of photos, videos and other files were reworked so that large files, or large batches of files, upload more reliably even at low internet speeds (4 March 2025); that an Uploading banner opens a screen showing progress and failed uploads, which can be retried together (31 July 2024); that photos taken in the Field Service app can be mapped to embed automatically in a report (16 September 2025); and that an upload custom field on a scheduled event can hold images, documents and videos added from the app (17 July 2026). No camera resolution requirement is published. Source: payaca.com

  • Forms, documents and customer signatures on site, in the app

    Forms have been completed natively in the mobile app rather than a browser since July 2022, and field agents can add a form to an event they are assigned to when the office has not set one up (7 August 2024). Forms with a customer signature section have a Customer not present checkbox (16 August 2022). From 12 June 2026, a field agent can open the Files screen on a scheduled event, tap plus, and create a document from any of the account's templates; Payaca fills it with the project's data, and if the template captures a signature the customer signs on the field agent's device. The vendor's forms guide (31 May 2025) says the office can pre-fill known details and that submitted data can pre-populate quotes, invoices and compliance documents. Source: payaca.com

  • Time logs with GPS verification and a location permission

    The mobile app page says engineers clock in and out with GPS verification and that timesheets are generated automatically for payroll and job costing. The Google Play listing's interactive elements include Shares location. The vendor's 30 September 2026 update says admins can choose which time log types staff can use outside an event, and that the app asks what comes next when an event ends. The vendor does not publish what location accuracy it needs from a device, or how the GPS check behaves when location is unavailable. Source: payaca.com

  • Windows: no Windows app, web app in a browser, no browser list published

    Payaca publishes no native Windows app. The office product is the web app at web.payaca.com, and the vendor's home page structured data lists Web, iOS and Android as its platforms. The only browser guidance we could find was a help centre article about iPad logouts that referred to Safari and Chrome, and that article no longer resolves. No supported browser list, browser version or PC specification is published. The Field Service app features the vendor documents (offline working, on-site documents and signatures, photo and file uploads from the device, GPS time logs) are described for the iOS and Android app, not the browser. Source: payaca.com

Payaca's site work is a day's events, time logs, a materials list, forms, documents signed on screen and a lot of photos, which fit an 8 inch screen without the bulk of a 10 inch tablet. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play against the Android 7.0 minimum the Google Play listing data gives, so it clears the only published platform figure by five major versions. The vendor's customers are solar, heat pump, battery and EV charger installers, and much of that work is outside: the A8's 1000 nit screen is the brightest of the Android devices, which matters when a customer signs a handover document in daylight or you check a materials list on a roof. Setting up

Getting Payaca running

  1. Ask your Payaca account owner to add the installer as a user and assign them the events they will work on. Payaca sells through a demo rather than a free trial, so check which features your plan includes before you buy devices.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install Field Service by Payaca (package com.payaca.fieldservice.mobile, developer Payaca), not the older Payaca mobile app, then sign in.
  3. Allow camera and location access when the app asks. The vendor documents photo and file uploads from the device and GPS verified clock in and out, and the Google Play listing says the app shares location.
  4. Fit a data SIM. The A8, A10 and A6 all take two SIMs, so a second network covers areas where the first is weak, which matters for the large photo and video uploads the vendor says the app sends.
  5. Before the first job without signal, open the app while online so it saves that day's and the next day's events, upcoming tasks and the materials catalogue to the device, as the vendor's update notes describe. Use the in-app refresh button after the schedule changes.
  6. Test the on-site flows on one unit: start and end a work time log, build a materials list, complete a form, take and upload a batch of photos, and generate and sign a document from the Files screen of an event, then check the Uploading screen to confirm nothing failed before rolling out to the team.
  7. On a Tuga W10, open the Payaca web app at web.payaca.com in Edge or Chrome and keep the browser updated. Use it for office work; it will not run the Field Service app.
  8. For the A8 and A10, fit the vehicle mounting dock in the van and a 12V car charger; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

Questions

Payaca on a Tuga device

Payaca publishes no system requirements page. The Google Play listing data for Field Service by Payaca gives a minimum API level of 24, which is Android 7.0, and the vendor publishes no RAM or storage figure for phones or tablets. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play and has 6GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it meets the only published figure, as do the A10 (Android 14, 8GB RAM) and the A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM). We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Payaca; these are the vendor's published figures set against the device specifications, so try the app on one unit before buying for a team.

The vendor says the Field Service app is built offline-first and syncs when back online. Its update notes list what that covers: the day's and next day's events and some tasks are saved to the device when you open the app, materials are stored on the device for building lists, confirming you are on the way, starting work and completing an event sync later, work time logs can be started and ended offline, and from June 2026 a document can be generated, filled in and signed without a signal. The A8, A10 and A6 all run that app. The vendor does not publish how much storage the cached data uses, and the web app on a Tuga W10 is not documented as working offline.

Yes. The vendor's June 2026 update says a field agent can create a document from any of the account's templates on a scheduled event, and if the template captures a signature the customer signs on the field agent's device, offline if needed. Forms with a signature section also have a Customer not present checkbox. The vendor does not say whether a finger or a stylus is expected. We sell a capacitive stylus for the A8, A10 and W10 at £14.99; it is not listed as compatible with the A6.

No barcode, QR code or NFC scanning by the device is documented in the vendor's Google Play listing, features page or update notes. Materials are chosen from a catalogue stored on the device, not scanned. So the Zebra 2D scan engine on the Tuga A6 and the NFC radio on the A8, A10 and A6 should not be treated as Payaca features, and you should not pick the A6 for its scanner on Payaca's account.

Both meet the published Android 7.0 minimum. The A8 has a 1000 nit screen against the A10's 350 nits, a removable battery, VESA mount points, and costs £379. The A10 has a larger, sharper 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen for multi-page handover documents and commissioning forms, 8GB RAM against 6GB, storage expandable to 2TB, IP68 against IP67 and MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not have, at £449. Installers who spend the day outdoors and run GPS time logs all day may prefer the A8; those filling in long documents or working in wetter, harder conditions are better served by the A10.
